adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:77 — Blacklist check compares raw guest input against lowercased list, so `Foo@Bar.com` trivially bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:52 — Any attendee (including one just added by another attendee) can add more guests, giving unbounded recursive spam amplification from Cal.com's domain with no rate limit or array-size cap.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation is an `authedProcedure` and explicitly authorizes any authenticated user who is an attendee (`const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find(...)` and then `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN`). That means once an email is added to `booking.attendees` (and if that email corresponds to a Cal.com account that can authenticate), that attendee can call `addGuests` again and add more guests. Additionally, `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` (`guests: z.array(z.string().email())`) and the handler impose no maximum length/cap on the guests array, so a caller can submit a very large list and trigger `sendAddGuestsEmails` fan-out to all attendees/team members. The specific claim about “no rate limit” cannot be proven from this diff alone, but the “any attendee can add guests” + “no array-size cap” spam-amplification vector is directly supported by the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — Email send failure is swallowed with a console.log and the mutation still returns success, so the UI shows "Guests added" while nobody was notified.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try/catch` that only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and does not rethrow or return an error. The handler then proceeds to `return { message: "Guests added" }`, so the TRPC mutation resolves successfully even when email delivery fails. On the client (`AddGuestsDialog`), `onSuccess` always shows `showToast(t("guests_added"), "success")` and closes the dialog, meaning the UI will indicate success while notifications may not have been sent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46 — Team permission uses isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner (should be OR) and passes teamId ?? 0 for non-team bookings, so team admins are wrongly denied and the check silently queries a bogus team id.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:20 — No check that the booking is not CANCELLED, REJECTED, or in the past, so guests can be attached to and mailed about dead bookings.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `addGuestsHandler`, the booking is fetched by `id` and then updated (`prisma.booking.update` with `attendees.createMany`) and notification emails/calendar updates are triggered, but there is no conditional guard based on booking lifecycle/state (e.g., cancelled/rejected) or time (e.g., `startTime` already passed). The handler only checks permissions and email uniqueness/blacklist. So, as written in the diff, it is possible to attach guests and send “guests added” emails for bookings that are no longer active (if such states exist on the booking model).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:101 — Duplicate filtering is read-then-write with no unique constraint or transaction, so concurrent requests create duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails.

adjudication.rationale: The handler does compute `uniqueGuests` by comparing against `booking.attendees` fetched earlier and then performs a separate `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`, so it is true this is a read-then-write pattern without an explicit transaction in the diff. However, the finding claims there is "no unique constraint" preventing duplicates, which cannot be verified from the provided diff (the database schema / Prisma model constraints are not shown). If a unique constraint exists (e.g., on bookingId+email) or `createMany` is configured elsewhere to skip duplicates, duplicates would not be created. Therefore the core claim that duplicates will be created is not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — Attendees are committed to the DB before updateCalendarAttendees; a throw there leaves guests persisted, calendar unsynced, and no emails sent while the client sees an error.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code first persists new attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterwards calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` (not inside a try/catch and not in a DB transaction). If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the TRPC mutation will error out to the client, but the DB changes (new attendees) have already been committed, leaving the booking updated while external calendars are unsynced. Since `sendAddGuestsEmails` is after that call, it also will not run when `updateCalendarAttendees` throws. This is a real partial-failure/consistency bug introduced by the ordering and lack of transactional/compensating logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/emails/email-manager.ts:541 — New-guest detection uses the raw `guests` input rather than the actually-inserted uniqueGuests, so an existing attendee resubmitted in the input gets a fresh "scheduled" email and blacklisted/dropped addresses are mis-classified.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out emails that are already attendees and any blacklisted emails, and only those are inserted via `createMany`. However it then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the raw input array `guests`, not `uniqueGuests`. In `sendAddGuestsEmails` (email-manager.ts), classification is based on `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` to decide which attendees receive a fresh `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Passing the raw input means an existing attendee email resubmitted in `guests` will be treated as a “new guest” and get the scheduled email again, even though they were not newly added. This is a concrete correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — Newly added guests receive AttendeeScheduledEmail containing videoCallData url/password and the full attendee list, leaking meeting credentials and co-attendee emails even for seated events.
packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:58 — findFirstOrThrow on `booking.userId || 0` throws an opaque 500 for bookings with a null userId (dynamic/team bookings).

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the organizer is fetched with `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } ... })`. The `|| 0` strongly indicates `booking.userId` can be null/undefined. If it is null, this will query for user id 0, which will not exist, causing `findFirstOrThrow` to throw (unhandled here), resulting in a generic 500. This can happen even when authorization passes via `isTeamAdminOrOwner` or `isAttendee`, since the organizer lookup is unconditional after those checks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:80 — When every submitted guest is a duplicate or blacklisted the error message is "emails_must_be_unique_valid", conflating a successful blacklist block with a validation error and hiding the real outcome.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out (a) emails already present in `booking.attendees` and (b) emails in `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`. If that filter removes all submitted guests, it throws `TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "emails_must_be_unique_valid" })`.
